target_customer: Airlines that rent or loan cinematic headsets to passengers, later lounges, trains, hotels and cruise ships
problem: Seatback screens are small and passengers on long flights want immersive private entertainment.
business_model: B2B subscription bundling headset hardware, content licensing, software and operations for airlines
product_category: Wearable cinematic VR headset for in-flight entertainment

founders.name: Laurence Fornari
previous_startups: An earlier startup, name not given on the YC page
founders.background_notes: YC page: over 15 years of B2B video technology sales to telecom companies, broadcasters and Hollywood studios; SkyLights is her second startup.

founders.name: David Dicko
founders.background_notes: CEO of SkyLights and of the merged SkyLights Inc per Apex (2018-11-08). Co-founder role per a Crunchbase person profile and a company profile seen in search results; Crunchbase could not be opened (403), so the co-founder title rests on search snippets.

exit.reason: Merger with Allomind announced 2018-11-08 under the name SkyLights Inc; Dicko stayed CEO and Allomind CEO Abhijit Limaye became chief product and technology officer.

competitors.name: Qantas with Samsung Gear VR
competitors.what: VR headsets offered to first class passengers and in lounges
competitors.traction_then: Pilot with Samsung; SkyLights positioned itself as complementary to seatback screens

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom headset hardware certified for aircraft, secure content delivery and film studio licensing made it a hardware plus content business.

defensibility.rationale: Airline certification and studio content deals created some friction, but rivals such as Inflight VR and Samsung pilots served the same airlines.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired it; SkyLights merged with headset maker Allomind in 2018.

market_need_then: In February 2016 XL Airways trialed eight headsets on four flights and reported a 99% satisfaction rating, with four more carriers lined up under NDA.

branding.domain_note: skylights.aero, an .aero sector domain; it did not resolve when fetched in 2026-11.
branding.brand_signature: Allosky, the second generation headset name co-launched with Allomind in June 2018

brand_strength.rationale: Trade and general press covered the headsets, and airline brands such as Air France, British Airways and Alaska used it, but no press about the SkyLights brand itself was found.

pivots.to: Merged company SkyLights Inc with Allomind, expanding to lounges, trains, hotels and cruise ships
pivots.why: The merger combined Allomind's optics and consumer product skills with SkyLights' airline relationships.

outcome_analysis: SkyLights, a Paris based in-flight cinematic headset maker, trialed with XL Airways in 2016 and later worked with Air France, British Airways and Alaska Airlines. It merged with Allomind in November 2018 into SkyLights Inc with Silicon Valley, Paris and Toulouse offices. No funding data or later shutdown was found, so the YC Inactive label is unexplained and failure factors stay empty. Several airline VR pilots from other vendors were later discontinued, but that is context.
notes: Two funding searches (company plus investors, and a French language search) and a Crunchbase query found no round; Crunchbase page appeared in results but its content was not readable, so funding is unknown, not zero. YC lists status Inactive while the merger record shows the company continued as SkyLights Inc after 2018; no source dates its end. Founded year per YC is 2016 but press shows XL Airways trials in February 2016, so 2015 is an estimate from that and may be wrong. David Dicko is named CEO of the merged company; Fornari is not mentioned in the merger article. Competitor list has one dated source. Audit fix: founded_year set to 2016 to match YC (the earlier 2015 estimate is superseded; a LinkedIn profile and one company profile say 2015, so the year is contested). David Dicko added as co-founder; a second source (Apex) confirms him as CEO but not as co-founder. Seed 2017-01: the audit cites Bouncewatch at about 1M EUR; Bouncewatch could not be opened, so the amount is left null (no currency conversion). The round rests on a single database family: Tracxn shows a Seed on 2017-01-19 with hidden amount, Crunchbase logs a seed on 2017-01-10 per search summary, and Fliarbi lists about 1M USD seed plus a separate 2017-01 grant of about 265K; treat as single-database, unverified amount. The earlier statement that no round was found is superseded. The exit is a merger with Allomind in Nov 2018 (Apex, 2018-11-08).
